STEP 1 - Scene: A single cooked chicken wing (appears to be a drumette/flat portion with the tip attached, pan-fried or roasted, with a brown crisp skin) on a white plate. Photographed from directly above on a dark tablecloth.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White plate with concentric rings, roughly a dinner/side plate. Estimating diameter ~25 cm (a typical dinner plate), so radius 12.5 cm, area = 3.14 x 12.5^2 ≈ 491 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: One chicken wing piece (skin-on, cooked), a small amount of rendered fat/oil sheen on the plate, and a tiny piece of crisp skin/meat near the lower left.

STEP 4 - Area: Wing ≈ 8% of plate area (about 40 cm^2; roughly 11 cm long by 4 cm wide at widest, scaled against the ~25 cm plate). Oil/fat sheen ≈ 0.5%. Small detached crumb ≈ 0.3%. Total food/fat coverage ≈ 9% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Wing ≈ 40 cm^2 x 1.5 cm average thickness = 60 ml. Oil sheen and crumb are negligible in volume (~2 ml combined).

STEP 6 - Grams: Wing 60 ml x 1.0 = ~60 g. Fat/oil ~1 g, crumb ~1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked chicken wing with skin, ~245 kcal/100 g (typical for roasted/fried skin-on wing meat). 60 g x 2.45 = ~147 kcal. Oil/fat residue ~1 g x 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 9 kcal. Crumb ~1 g x 250 kcal/100 g ≈ 3 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single skin-on chicken wing piece weighing roughly 50–70 g cooked, with about 150 kcal, is plausible for what is visible. Trace fat and crumbs add little. The total of ~63 g and ~160 kcal fits a single wing.
